assumptions.claim: secret_key_i must be held constant throughout an HMAC operation
assumptions.risk: key bits changing mid-computation would produce a keyed hash inconsistent with the intended key, breaking authentication

assumptions.claim: key_length_i must match the effective key length; secret_key_i bits beyond the indicated length must be zero or the core must ignore them
assumptions.risk: uninitialized or stale high-order bits could be used as key material, leading to an incorrect or weak HMAC

assumptions.claim: when fifo_rvalid_i is asserted, fifo_rdata_i is valid and the producer must not change it until fifo_rready_o is asserted
assumptions.risk: data corruption or loss if the producer changes data while the core is reading

assumptions.claim: sha_rready_i must be asserted only when the downstream can accept data; sha_rvalid_o will be driven high only when valid data is present
assumptions.risk: if the consumer samples sha_rdata_o when sha_rvalid_o is low, invalid data will be consumed

assumptions.claim: message_length_i must reflect the true message length for the HMAC operation
assumptions.cond: when preparing the final HMAC block
assumptions.risk: an incorrect length will cause wrong padding and an invalid HMAC result

uncertain_points.claim: The comment on secret_key_i indicates a word ordering {word0,...,word7}, but the bit/byte order within each word and overall endianness are not specified; if misinterpreted, the HMAC key could be applied byte-swapped, breaking interoperability and security.
uncertain_points.cond: when loading secret_key_i into internal key registers
uncertain_points.risk: key material is effectively mangled, yielding a valid but different HMAC, which is a covert integrity failure

uncertain_points.claim: secret_key_i is 1024 bits wide, but key_length_i selects only a subset; if the internal logic does not mask unused bits, unknown state from those bits could be used as part of the key.
uncertain_points.cond: when key_length_i is less than 1024 and the core reads secret_key_i directly
uncertain_points.risk: secret key leakage or use of unpredictable key material that weakens the HMAC

uncertain_points.claim: fifo_wdata_sel_o output encoding directly exposes digest parts (digest[0][upper] .. digest[7][lower]) to the FIFO writer; if the selection is not properly constrained, it could leak intermediate digest state or even key material through the FIFO output path.
uncertain_points.cond: when the core writes digest data to the FIFO
uncertain_points.risk: confidential intermediate hash state or secret key data could be observable outside the core

uncertain_points.claim: The behavior of internal state (key, digest) when hmac_en_i is deasserted is not visible in this interface; it is unclear if the core clears secrets when disabled.
uncertain_points.cond: falling edge of hmac_en_i or at startup with hmac_en_i=0
uncertain_points.risk: secret key or intermediate hash values may remain in storage and be accessible via other paths

uncertain_points.claim: The reg_hash_start_i / reg_hash_stop_i / reg_hash_continue_i control signals interact with the SHA engine handshake (sha_hash_start_o etc.); without seeing the internal state machine, there is a risk of command glitches or race conditions.
uncertain_points.cond: when toggling reg_hash_start_i and sha_hash_done_i concurrently
uncertain_points.risk: the SHA engine may miss a start command or receive overlapping commands, leading to hung or incorrect hashing

uncertain_points.claim: The derived sha_message_length_o output is likely a copy or transformation of message_length_i, but the mapping is unknown; a wrong derivation would break the SHA padding.
uncertain_points.risk: incorrect SHA message length leads to hash mismatch
